props.title: Séance

sections.content: Kiyoshi Kurosawa's **Séance** (2000) represents a pivotal moment in Japanese horror cinema, arriving during the peak of J-horror's international influence. Following the success of **Ringu** (1998) and **Ju-On: The Grudge** (2002), Kurosawa's adaptation of Mark McShane's novel "Séance on a Wet Afternoon" transplants British supernatural noir into distinctly Japanese territory. The film's methodical pacing and emphasis on atmospheric dread over jump scares showcases Kurosawa's signature style, which he perfected in Cure (1997) and Pulse (2001).

movies.title: Cure
movies.slug: A detective investigates a series of murders where the killers have no memory of their crimes. Kurosawa's psychological horror masterpiece.

movies.title: Pulse
movies.slug: Technology becomes a portal for loneliness and death in this prescient horror about internet-age isolation.

sections.content: The film's focus on a psychic medium and her husband's descent into moral corruption echoes similar themes in **The Sixth Sense** (1999) and **What Lies Beneath** (2000), but with Kurosawa's distinct sociological perspective. The director's exploration of marriage and isolation would later influence films like Dark Water (2002) and **A Tale of Two Sisters** (2003), where domestic spaces become sites of supernatural anxiety.

The technical craft in **Séance** (2000) demonstrates Kurosawa's mastery of subtle horror. His use of negative space and long, static shots creates unbearable tension, similar to techniques employed in **Kairo** (2001) and later perfected in **Tokyo Sonata** (2008). The film's sound design, with its emphasis on silence punctuated by unsettling ambient noise, established a template for contemporary atmospheric horror like **The Others** (2001) and **Lake Mungo** (2008). SUBHEAD: Impact on Modern Horror

movies.title: Dark Water
movies.slug: A single mother and her daughter move into a haunted apartment with a mysterious water leak. A masterpiece of atmospheric horror.

sections.content: **Séance** (2000) helped establish the contemplative horror movement that influenced films like **The Orphanage** (2007) and **I Am the Pretty Thing That Lives in the House** (2016). Its exploration of mediumship and the exploitation of supernatural abilities provides a more nuanced take than western counterparts like **White Noise** (2005) or **Insidious** (2010).
